attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated as his updated hypothesis. The NYT quote that follows is separate and not used as the claim.

semantics.note: 'I believe ... will have to raise ... by July 2025' is an unqualified expectation of a definite outcome, so it is scored. The normalisation keeps the antecedent (current round closing), the size floor and the horizon. Dropping the 'need' nuance is acceptable because the contract scores whether a raise happened.

contract.note: Reading 'by July 2025' as through 2025-07-31 and counting an announced round backed by a signed agreement is fair. The $40B round is far above the threshold and well inside the window, so no reading changes the result.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own dated announcement (2025-03-31) of $40B in new funding, inside the horizon and above $6.5-7B. It is a company disclosure, which the contract allows as a source.
The lead investor disclosed a definitive agreement signed 2025-03-31 for up to $40B, with a $10B first closing planned for mid-April 2025. This meets the contract's investor-disclosure requirement.

output.rationale: The October 2024 round closed, and on 2025-03-31 OpenAI announced a $40B round. SoftBank disclosed a signed agreement with a $10B first closing planned for April 2025. This is a new round larger than $6.5-7B, inside the July 2025 horizon, so the support condition is met. The packet contains no counterevidence.
